Have you ever found yourself caught between the beliefs you grew up with and the person you’re becoming? Questions about faith, identity, and where we truly belong can feel especially personal when they’re tangled up with family stories and cultural traditions.
That’s exactly the journey we’ll be exploring together, inspired by Lisa See’s heartfelt work, Committed: A Skeptic Makes Peace with His Parents' Religion. In this story, curiosity and skepticism walk hand-in-hand, as we navigate the delicate balance between honoring our roots and searching for our own meaning.
We’ll step into a world where family ties and rituals pull us one way, while our own questions tug us in another. What does it take to reconcile a secular outlook with generations of tradition? How do moments of doubt and discovery shape who we are—and who we want to become?
As we go deeper, you’ll notice how every conversation, every ritual, and each flicker of uncertainty becomes a chance for connection, reflection, and growth. It’s not about finding all the answers, but about opening ourselves up to the questions—and letting them shape our journey.
So, as we embark on this exploration, let’s keep our minds open and our hearts curious. Together, we’ll discover just how powerful it can be to make peace, not by solving every mystery, but by embracing the search itself.
